rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation is in hardsigmoid_kernel_scalar (line 48). The kernel selection logic uses: if (size >= 1024) → vectorized kernel, else → scalar kernel. Fixed input shape [16, 16384] gives size = 262144. Since 262144 >= 1024, only the vectorized kernel executes. The scalar kernel containing the mutation is NEVER called.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes threadIdx.x to threadIdx.z in the scalar kernel. However, the scalar kernel is only invoked when the tensor has fewer than 1024 elements (size < 1024). With the fixed input shape of [16, 16384], the tensor has 262144 elements, which is far greater than 1024. Therefore, the code always takes the vectorized kernel path (hardsigmoid_kernel_vectorized), which is completely unchanged by this mutation. The mutated code in hardsigmoid_kernel_scalar is unreachable under the fixed-shape contract, making any value-level input incapable of triggering the mutation. This explains why Layer 2's 112 test rounds all produced bitwise identical outputs.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation resides in the scalar kernel which only executes when size < 1024. The fixed input shape [16, 16384] has 262144 elements, ensuring the vectorized kernel (unaffected by the mutation) is always used. To kill this mutant, one would need to reduce the tensor to fewer than 1024 elements, which violates the fixed-shape constraint.
rounds.recommendations: When mutating GPU kernels, mutation testing tools should consider kernel dispatch conditions. This mutation in the scalar fallback kernel is semantically dead code for the tested configuration. Test coverage should include explicit tests that exercise all kernel dispatch paths - in this case, a separate small-tensor test (size < 1024) would be needed to exercise the scalar kernel. Consider adding shape-parameterized tests to ensure all kernel code paths are covered.
